audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 4-5 and 6 were scored Skill against whys that say you keep the poke edge and own the wave, and that Slicing Maelstrom kills him. The 2+ item row was scored Kennen while its own why ends 'the lane is his'.
audit.why: 52.9% over 707 games: Kennen holds every stage from level 2 to first item on 950-range poke against a 775/400-range kit, and gives it back only at full build.
audit.corrected: Rows 3 and 4 flipped to Kennen, row 6 to Sylas, in matched pairs — which is also the packet chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hijack was treated as a permanent threat with no timing attached.
audit.why: It is 80/55/30 — at rank 1 an 80-second cooldown, which is a real 80-second window to fight in, and by rank 3 it is 30s and effectively always available. That difference is the whole shape of the matchup and no field stated it.
audit.corrected: 80s at rank 1 written into mid, whys[4] and breakdown.cooldowns; the 30s rank-3 figure into spikes[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: Six fields describe Abscond/Abduct as a 'dash + stun' or an 'E-chain stun', and late says it 'interrupts your R channel'.
audit.why: Riot's text: Sylas dashes to a location and can recast to throw his chains, pulling HIMSELF to an enemy he hits. There is no stun and no CC of any kind on it — it is a gap-closer that re-engages you, which is a different problem needing a different answer. Slicing Maelstrom also carries no channel flag, so nothing about the ability interrupts it.
audit.corrected: Restated everywhere as a 400-range dash on 13s whose recast chains him back onto you.

audit.whatIsWrong: Kingslayer is only ever called 'Q-W drain' and Grievous Wounds never appears in the content layer.
audit.why: Kingslayer is the heal — it only heals against enemy champions, and its cooldown falls from 12s to 6s with ranks, so by mid-game he is healing off you every six seconds. Oblivion Orb timing decides whether your chip is real damage or free healing for him.
audit.corrected: Named as Kingslayer throughout and Oblivion Orb written into wants.you[1] and early.

edits.before: Sylas wants to sit in the wave and heal your poke off with his Q-W drain, so don't trade into a full-health Sylas expecting damage to stick — it won't. Instead farm with max-range Q (Thundering Shuriken) and only commit a stun when he steps up to melee a minion: a Q-mark plus an Electrical Surge auto, then E-in for the third stack stuns him through his own setup. Watch his E (chain-dash) — if you E onto him while his is up, he just dashes free and Q-W drains the fight back even.
edits.after: Sylas sits in the wave and heals your poke off with Chain Lash and Kingslayer, so don't trade into a full-health Sylas expecting damage to stick — it won't, and an early Oblivion Orb is what fixes that. Farm with max-range Q (Thundering Shuriken) and commit a stun only when he steps up to melee a minion: a Q-mark plus an Electrical Surge auto, then E-in for the third stack. Watch Abscond (E, 13s) — E onto him while it is up and he dashes free, then heals the trade back even.

edits.before: This is your window. Your Q poke chips faster than his drain heals once you have a few autos of Electrical Surge sustained on-hit, and at 6 your Slicing Maelstrom stun-locks him for a kill before Q-W can out-sustain it. The catch that makes this lane real: Sylas's R steals YOUR ultimate. If he R-steals before you channel, he gets his own Slicing Maelstrom — so bait his R with a fake E-in, or fully commit only when his R is down. With Hextech Alternator your Q-W-E-R combo blows up his squishy AP body outright.
edits.after: This is your window. Your Q poke chips faster than Kingslayer heals once Electrical Surge on-hit is running, and at 6 your Slicing Maelstrom stun-locks him for a kill before he heals it off. The catch that makes this lane real: Hijack steals YOUR ultimate from 950 range on 80s at rank 1. If he takes it first he gets his own Slicing Maelstrom — so bait it with a fake E-in, or commit only while those 80 seconds run. With Hextech Alternator your Q-W-E-R blows up his squishy body outright.

edits.before: Once Sylas hits 2+ items the lane flips — his Q-W drain out-sustains your burst, his E-chain stun interrupts your R channel and E-in, and a stolen ultimate gives him a second game-changing button you don't have an answer to. You're a fragile short-cooldown caster who gets focused down the moment your R is on cooldown. Win this on your 6 and first-item spike, take plates and a kill, and pivot to teamfighting where your AoE R peels — do not try to 1v1 a fed Sylas in the sidelane.
edits.after: Once Sylas hits 2+ items the lane flips — Kingslayer out-heals your burst on a 6s cooldown, Abduct chains him straight back onto you the moment you walk away, and a stolen ultimate gives him a second game-changing button you have no answer to. You're a fragile short-cooldown caster who gets focused the moment your R is down. Win this on your 6 and first-item spike, take plates and a kill, and pivot to teamfighting where your AoE R peels — never 1v1 a fed Sylas in the sidelane.

notes: Abscond/Abduct was described as a 'dash + stun' in six fields. It has no CC at all: Sylas dashes, and the recast throws chains that pull HIM to the enemy hit. Corrected everywhere, along with the usual 'interrupts your R channel' claim (Slicing Maelstrom has no channel flag). Hijack's 80/55/30 was never on the page and it is the number that decides when you may commit — at rank 1 you get a genuine 80-second window, by rank 3 you effectively never do. packet.suspectNames flags 'Your Slicing Maelstrom' in spikes[1] as a probable wrong ability name; that is a false positive — the string is 'Your Slicing Maelstrom all-in', which is Kennen's own correctly-named ultimate.
